name: Elymus

project_scope.selection_mode: Genus comparison lesson from live Master Plant Pool and existing Poaceae family module
project_scope.admission_note: Both taxa occur in the approved Master Plant Pool. This lesson does not install taxa or change settled range status.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Confirm a true grass at the node/collar, then move to the spike: Elymus has a narrow spike with spikelets attached along the central rachis. For these two species, inspect the spikelet/glume-awn package and whether the spike is strongly nodding or more erect before trusting general habit.
shared_genus_characters.vegetative: Perennial cool-season grasses with jointed culms, leaf sheaths/blades and a ligule at the collar.
shared_genus_characters.reproductive: Inflorescence a terminal spike; spikelets sit along the rachis and contain multiple florets. Glumes and lemmas/awns carry the useful species characters.
shared_genus_characters.genus_confirmation: Node + sheath/collar/ligule confirms the grass doorway; a true terminal spike with multi-flowered spikelets along the rachis moves the learner into Elymus rather than the branched-panicle grasses.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: Whole spike posture, then awns/glumes at one intact spikelet
species_comparison_matrix.architecture: Mature spikes commonly arch or nod conspicuously and have a long-bristly appearance from spreading/curving awns.
species_comparison_matrix.spikelet: Use the long conspicuous lemma awns and the glume/awn package as reproductive confirmation.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: A strongly nodding mature spike with long spreading/curving awns is the fast field door; confirm on an intact spikelet.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Do not identify from 'nodding' alone—wind, maturity and damage change posture.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: Whole spike posture, then glumes/awns at one intact spikelet
species_comparison_matrix.architecture: Spike is typically more erect/straight and visually tighter than Canada wildrye; awns are less dramatically spreading.
species_comparison_matrix.spikelet: Confirm with the comparatively compact spikelet/glume-awn architecture rather than leaf width or color.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: More erect compact spike + less dramatically spreading awns favors E. virginicus; reproductive close-up should confirm.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Vegetative plants are unsafe for a forced species ID in this two-species lesson.

decision_sequence: Confirm Poaceae at a real culm node and collar/ligule.
Find a mature terminal spike and photograph the whole spike before zooming in.
Strongly nodding/arching, shaggy spike with long spreading/curving awns → E. canadensis door.
More erect/compact spike with less dramatically spreading awns → E. virginicus door.
Zoom to one intact spikelet and document glumes, florets and awns before finalizing.
If only leaves are present or the reproductive characters conflict, leave the plant at Elymus and route the observation to Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review.
overlap_and_cautions: Spike posture is a fast first split, not a stand-alone proof.
Leaf width, plant height, green color and habitat overlap and should remain supporting context only.
Broken or immature spikes can erase the strongest visual differences; require an intact mature reproductive unit for difficult plants.
Do not use generic 'wild rye' gestalt when spikelet structures are available.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Compare the spikelet arrangement at each rachis node and the bristly awn architecture; photograph a node-level spikelet cluster rather than relying on the fuzzy silhouette.
Use an intact spikelet to document glumes, number of florets and awn origin; branched panicles exit the Elymus doorway immediately.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Teach the quickest field split without relying on color.
Tie the fast silhouette cue to reproductive structure.
Teach what makes this a spike and separate look-alike spike grasses.
Reinforce the grass/genus workflow before species separation.
Prevent false confidence from overlapping leaves/habit.

media_routing.existing_project_media: Reuse exact Elymus project/user/Joey media only when it clearly shows one of the listed diagnostic roles.
media_routing.instruction: Highest-value acquisition is a matched mature-spike pair plus intact spikelet macros; generic meadow/habit photos are secondary.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: Verify difficult/intermediate Elymus material from an intact mature spikelet; do not force species from leaves alone.
Species taxonomy/range certification and canonical installation remain outside this lane.

sources.supports: grass anatomy, collar/ligule workflow and spikelet terminology
approved source-pool membership for E. canadensis and E. virginicus
